shots.words: Try to tickle yourself. Go on.
Your fingers touch the same skin, but almost nothing happens.
That is not because your hands are bad at tickling.
shots.acting: accuses own hands; hands look offended

shots.words: Before you move, your brain sends a prediction to a region called the cerebellum.
It estimates where your fingers will land and turns down the expected sensation.
Now let someone else try. Their timing, pressure, and direction are unpredictable.
shots.acting: friend hides moving hands; Mira suspicious

shots.words: The prediction misses, the alarm stays loud, and suddenly you are twisting like a malfunctioning noodle.
shots.acting: large C-to-S body reaction; hair and sleeves overlap

shots.words: Your brain did not stop the touch. It spoiled the surprise.
shots.acting: Mira points to surprise gift held by brain
